title: UK Urged to Build 'Trade Bazooka' Against Trump

lines: Trump threatened UK with tariffs last week.
He demands Britain drop its digital services tax.
US tech companies say the tax unfairly targets them.
Tensions between nations are rapidly escalating now.
British Chambers of Commerce issued urgent warning today.
UK's economic security is dangerously inadequate, they say.
Years of government neglect have left Britain vulnerable.
Growth and jobs are now at serious risk.
Global crises have battered British companies for years.
Brexit, Covid, Ukraine war, Middle East conflict.
International trade has become increasingly fraught and unstable.
UK firms struggle to navigate this hostile landscape.
Business leaders want government to act decisively now.
They're calling for an EU-style 'trade bazooka.'
This tool would deter economic coercion attempts.
Brussels uses it to protect against bullying tactics.
EU's anti-coercion instrument restricts trade with aggressors.
It limits goods, services, and financial market access.
Property rights and foreign investment can be blocked.
Public procurement programmes become unavailable to offenders.
New UK legislation would need broad ministerial powers.
Tariffs, market access, investment scrutiny all included.
Subsidy controls would strengthen Britain's negotiating position.
Safeguards must protect legitimate UK commercial interests.
Government minister Chris Bryant acknowledged the report's findings.
He confirmed UK is exploring last-resort defensive tools.
Diplomacy remains the preferred approach for now.
Britain seeks to keep markets open and secure.
Retaliation against US carries significant economic risks.
America is Britain's largest single trading partner.
US firms have invested over £640 billion here.
One-fifth of UK trade flows to America.
